messages:
marco: Quick Q — pushed a Terraform change that creates an IAM role + IRSA for a service account in the payments namespace (billing-worker). Pod is still getting the default node role, not the IRSA role. Any quick debug steps?

alice: Can you paste the SA yaml and the TF role ARN? often it's just a mismatch in the annotation key or the role trust policy.

marco: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482
Here is the SA created by our Helm chart (values didn't include the annotation):

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: billing-worker
  namespace: payments
  labels:
    app: billing
```

marco: TF created role: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/infra-payments-billing-worker

alice: ok — first things: 1) verify the annotation key is exactly `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` on the SA that the pod uses, 2) ensure the role's trust policy includes the cluster OIDC provider and `sub` condition `system:serviceaccount:payments:billing-worker`.

alice: quick commands:
`kubectl -n payments get sa billing-worker -o yaml`
`kubectl -n payments get pod <pod-name> -o yaml | grep -A3 serviceAccount`

jon: I skimmed the PR — Helm chart creates the SA but our values override was missing. So the TF role exists but the annotation never made it onto the SA (Helm overwrote). Also make sure it's not using a projected token from a different SA via podSpec.serviceAccountName mismatch.

sarah: From inside a pod you can run `aws sts get-caller-identity` (requires awscli) to see which role is assumed. If it returns the node role, then SA annotation either missing or trust policy wrong.

marco: tried `kubectl describe sa billing-worker -n payments` and saw no annotations. I patched it manually and the pod picked up the role after restart. Patch used: 

```bash
kubectl -n payments patch sa billing-worker -p '{"metadata": {"annotations": {"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/infra-payments-billing-worker"}}}'
```

marco: But want to fix by default in infra code — looks like Helm chart needs to accept `serviceAccount.annotations` in values. Should I update the chart or add a k8s manifest in TF apply?

alice: Prefer updating the Helm values so chart remains authoritative. If chart doesn't support annotations, add a small `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` patch in the module or submit a PR to the chart.

jon: Also check Secrets Store CSI driver: if you're mounting secrets via the driver it uses the pod's SA for K8s RBAC, but IRSA is separate. Just verifying you didn't mix up which identity is used for secret provider access. For AWS Secrets Manager provider, the pod still assumes the same IRSA role.

marco: Good point — we're using secrets-store-csi and provider-aws. After the SA annotation patch the CSI driver was able to call GetSecret.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: helm release payments/billing upgraded (chart v2.3.1) — canary rollout started.

marco: I'll open a follow-up PR to add annotations to the Helm values and add a unit test that ensures our staging cluster SA has the role-arn annotated. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sarah: Nice — adding the trust policy check to the TF module would also catch missing OIDC provider condition in future.

marco: added TODO in the PR and pinged @alice for review. Thanks everyone.
